corrections.finding: Stronger than source and than item 4: 'An animal self' has a through-tunnel and a shell or skeleton only in many animals. 'carbon going through, ingesting and exhausting' makes carbon the one ingesting, against Chemistry 1.6 (carbon a non-living stable form, a nothing its couplings surround; the body ingests). 'protecting cores' is not in the nucleosome source (histone cores).
corrections.fixed_text: In many animals a self lives with three stable forms: a genome inside each cell, an artifact of prior living, spiralling around its histone cores; carbon going through, a body's ingesting and exhausting of it along a tunnel opening through the body at its forming; and a shell or skeleton outside, a stable form the animal lays from its inception, a conch's spiral the clearest. Inside, through and outside, each a stable form a living goes on with and none a living, and between each stable form and its neighbour a supple between, protein, water, a weak sharing, taking each changing, and no stable form inflicting a changing on another while they co-exist. A possible tri-cycling of stable forms around one living self, pattern and gap, its involutioning at a body's forming.

corrections.finding: Stronger than source: 'Nacre's tablets' generalises one species (Pinna nobilis nacre, not the conch) to all nacre; 'cracks along its layers' interfaces' should be lamellar interfaces and they dissipate energy; shielding of microcracks is in the outer layers only; 'it springs back' has no clear subject (tablets, layer or nacre).
corrections.fixed_text: A conch's shell, Strombus gigas, is some 99 percent aragonite, a calcium carbonate, and under 1 percent protein, three mineral layers in a crossed lamellar structure with a protein matrix between them; it is 10 to 30 times stronger than pure aragonite and as much as 1,000 times tougher, many cracks along its lamellar interfaces dissipating energy, and in its outer layers microcracks shielding each other, its middle layer's lamellae going as reinforcing bars. The nacre of Pinna nobilis has tablets a few hundred nanometres across in a thin organic layer: under a force the organic layer moves aside and the tablets lock together, and when the force goes the nacre springs back, losing none of its resilience over impact after impact up to 80 percent of its yield strength, a crack staying within one layer. Hard pieces and a supple between, pattern and gap: the between takes a changing, and the pieces co-exist with no piece inflicting a changing on its neighbour.

corrections.finding: Stronger than source: 'each strand going on whole' at replication overstates (source and textbook give only: backbone covalent within strands, strands separate and re-anneal); 'A genome's stable form spirals around protecting cores' makes every genome and all its DNA nucleosomal (146 bp wraps are stretches, in cells with histones) and 'protecting' is not in the source.
corrections.fixed_text: In the cells of an animal a genome's stable form spirals in stretches around histone cores: about 146 base pairs of DNA wind 1.65 turns, a left-handed superhelix, around a histone octamer, two each of H2A, H2B, H3 and H4. Within a double helix two strands go in opposite directions, A with T and G with C, each strand's sequence the other's complement, a male and a female piece; along each strand its links are strong and between the strands its sharing is weak, and the two strands co-exist, opening apart and coming together again, each strand's own links staying strong through the opening. A bi-connector of complementary pieces, protecting by spiralling, a weak between taking the changing.

corrections.finding: Stronger than source: cells rolling in over a lip is Xenopus gastrulation, stated as gastrulation in general; and the through-gut from mouth to anus is not open at gastrulation but follows it, and only in many animals.
corrections.fixed_text: At gastrulation in Xenopus a ball of cells folds inward, cells rolling in over a lip, a field's own word involution; in many animals the gut that follows runs through a body from mouth to anus: a sphere of genus nought forming as a body of genus one, a torus, its tunnel the way of ingesting and exhausting. A body's natural torusing is physical at its forming, involutioning and volution together, co-chaining along its tunnel and bi-tunneling across its surface, carbon going through it.
